definitions.explanation: Describes something that has no apparent end or limit, either literally (in physical extent) or figuratively (in duration, scope, or intensity).

examples.japanese: {果|は}てしない{大地|だいち}が{広|ひろ}がっている。
{果|は}てしない{議論|ぎろん}が{続|つづ}いている。
{宇宙|うちゅう}の{果|は}てしない{広|ひろ}がりを{想像|そうぞう}すると、{自分|じぶん}の{小|ちい}ささを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: When I imagine the boundless expanse of the universe, I feel how small I am.

notes:
Derived from {果|は}てる (to end, to be exhausted) + しない (not). Literally 'does not end.' Despite being formed from a verb, it functions as an i-adjective and modifies nouns directly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {果|は}てしない{旅|たび}: an endless journey
- {果|は}てしない{議論|ぎろん}: an endless debate
- {果|は}てしない{努力|どりょく}: endless effort
- {果|は}てしない{広|ひろ}がり: boundless expanse
- {果|は}てしなく{続|つづ}く: to continue endlessly

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {終|お}わりのない: never-ending — more everyday and conversational; {果|は}てしない is more literary and evocative
- {限|かぎ}りない: limitless, boundless — very similar; slightly more formal
- {永遠|えいえん}の: eternal — focuses on time; {果|は}てしない can apply to space, time, or abstract concepts
- {際限|さいげん}のない: unlimited — more formal; often used for quantities or processes
